title: AXI4 Address Attributes: Meaning and DV Risk
description: Inspect each Ax attribute to separate protocol encoding from system policy and see which address handshake captures it.

signals.name: AxPROT
signals.description: AWPROT or ARPROT labels privilege, security, and instruction/data intent. Bit 0 selects unprivileged/privileged, bit 1 secure/non-secure, and bit 2 data/instruction.
signals.direction: Master → interconnect and slave on AW or AR
signals.sampled: With the corresponding AW or AR handshake
signals.verificationNote: The protocol carries the attribute; the system address map defines the access policy and whether denial is generated by an interconnect or target.

signals.name: AxCACHE
signals.description: AWCACHE or ARCACHE describes Bufferable and Modifiable behavior plus read/write allocation hints. AXI4 renamed bit 1 from Cacheable to Modifiable while retaining the required behavior.
signals.direction: Master → interconnect and slave on AW or AR
signals.sampled: With the corresponding AW or AR handshake
signals.typicalUse: Select ordering, buffering, transformation, and cache-allocation behavior
signals.verificationNote: Do not decode AxCACHE as a single cacheable boolean. Check the complete encoding and AXI revision in scope.

signals.name: AxQOS
signals.description: AWQOS or ARQOS is a 4-bit transaction identifier. AXI recommends treating larger values as higher priority, but the exact scheduling policy is not specified by the protocol.
signals.direction: Master → interconnect and slave on AW or AR
signals.sampled: With the corresponding AW or AR handshake
signals.typicalUse: Provide a traffic-priority indication to a configured fabric
signals.verificationNote: Verify the product's documented QoS policy and starvation bounds; do not assert that AXI alone mandates one arbitration result.

signals.name: AxREGION
signals.description: Optional AWREGION or ARREGION identifies one of up to 16 logical regions that share a physical slave interface, allowing different logical interfaces to reuse overlapping addresses.
signals.direction: Master/interconnect → slave on AW or AR
signals.sampled: With the corresponding AW or AR handshake
signals.typicalUse: Distinguish logical register or memory regions behind one interface
signals.verificationNote: AxREGION is not a replacement for system address decoding. Verify the configured region mapping and default value when the signal is absent.

signals.name: AxLOCK
signals.expansion: Normal or Exclusive access in AXI4
signals.description: AWLOCK or ARLOCK is one bit in AXI4: 0 selects Normal and 1 selects Exclusive. Exclusive success is conditional and reported with EXOKAY; the attribute does not mandate a global lock.
signals.direction: Master → interconnect and slave on AW or AR
signals.sampled: With the corresponding AW or AR handshake
signals.verificationNote: Gate checking by revision and exclusive-support contract; distinguish successful EXOKAY from unsuccessful exclusive-write OKAY.

signals.name: AxUSER
signals.description: AWUSER and ARUSER carry optional system-defined request metadata. WUSER, RUSER, and BUSER can extend the other channel payloads; AXI does not define their system meaning.
signals.direction: Travels with the source-driven payload on the applicable channel
signals.typicalUse: Implementation-defined routing, tracing, or policy metadata
signals.verificationNote: When present, include USER bits in stability, correlation, and end-to-end checks without inventing protocol semantics.
